headline: Music activates more brain regions than almost any other human activity
universal_truth: Music is a universal language that speaks to something ancient in us
fun_facts: The oldest known musical instruments are 40,000-year-old flutes carved from bone
Music releases dopamine twice—once in anticipation, once at the emotional peak
Babies respond to rhythm before they can speak; it's one of our earliest cognitive abilities
discussion_questions: What song immediately takes you back to a specific moment in time?
Why do you think music can bring people to tears?
What role does music play in your daily life?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: A song comes on and suddenly you're 16 again, in a specific place, feeling exactly what you felt then. Music does something no other art form can—it hijacks your brain and transports you through time. Why does it have this power?

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Music seems useless from an evolutionary perspective. It doesn't feed us, protect us, or help us reproduce directly. Yet every culture in history has made music. Why would evolution preserve something so 'pointless'?
cliff.prompt: Why did humans evolve to love music?

options.text: It strengthens social bonds and group coordination
options.response: Yes. Music synchronizes groups, builds trust, and creates collective identity.

options.text: It's a byproduct of language and pattern recognition
options.response: There's overlap with language, but music seems to have its own purpose...

q1.title: Ancient Melodies
q1.script: The oldest known instruments are 40,000-year-old bone flutes from Germany. Music predates agriculture, writing, and possibly even language as we know it. Our ancestors made music before they settled in villages. It's that fundamental.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Ancient Melodies"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Double Dopamine
q2.script: Brain scans show music releases dopamine in two waves: first during anticipation of a favorite part, then again at the emotional peak. It's one of the few activities that rewards you both for expecting pleasure and experiencing it.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Babies Got Rhythm
q3.script: Infants respond to musical rhythm before they can speak or walk. They'll move to a beat and show distress when rhythms are disrupted. Music processing is one of the earliest cognitive abilities to emerge—wired into us from birth.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Music reminds us that we're more than thinking machines. We're beings who can be moved by vibrations in air arranged in patterns. That's not weakness—that's the beautiful complexity of being human.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 25. Tomorrow, we'll discover the power of asking good questions. Until then, put on a song you love—and let yourself be moved.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Musical Presence - Deep Listening
growTrack.learning_objective: Experience music with full attention and awareness
growTrack.activity: Choose one song and listen to it with complete attention—no multitasking, no phone, eyes closed if possible. Notice instruments, lyrics, dynamics, how it makes you feel. This is how music was meant to be experienced.
